data.name: Panini
data.gender_notes: Panini is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Panini is a Sanskrit name derived from the sage Panini, who is considered the father of Sanskrit grammar and the founder of the Ashtadhyayi, a text on Sanskrit grammar. This name is a symbol of knowledge, wisdom, and scholarship. The name Panini carries the meaning “Grammairian, Scholar” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Panini usually hope their child will grow to embody grammairian, scholar and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of knowledge and wisdom in Hindu tradition.
data.etymology: Panini belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grammairian, Scholar.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Panini total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Panini is a highly revered name in Hindu culture, associated with the great sage and linguistic genius who shaped the Sanskrit language. His contributions to Sanskrit grammar have had a profound impact on Indian literature and the preservation of ancient Hindu texts and traditions. The name Panini signifies a deep connection with the intellectual heritage and linguistic richness of Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Panini carries significant spiritual weight, representing a deep commitment to knowledge, wisdom, and the pursuit of understanding. The name evokes the image of the sage who spent his life devoted to deciphering the mysteries of language and unlocking the secrets of the Sanskrit language. Panini symbolizes the idea that true spiritual growth comes through deep knowledge and understanding, and that wisdom is a powerful force for enlightenment and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Panini is known as the architect of the Sanskrit language. His work, the Ashtadhyayi, laid the foundation for the systematic study of Sanskrit grammar. Symbolically, Panini represents clarity, order, and knowledge in language and communication. spiritually, he embodies the pursuit of wisdom, understanding, and the power of words to shape reality.
